title: Regulatory & Legal Risk Playbook — Private Deployment Sell Deck (sketch)
content:
Slide 1 — Purpose
One-line: A short sales deck to arm sellers and SEs for conversations with legal/compliance teams about Private and VPC deployments.
Goal: shorten procurement cycles by pre-empting legal objections and offering concrete controls/contract levers.
Audience: Legal, Security, Platform Architects, Procurement.

Slide 2 — Quick framing for execs (30s)
- Risk posture summary: Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) reduce legal/data residency risk by giving customers network & key control while preserving Redwood operational tooling when authorized.
- Key customer outcomes: auditable logs, certifiable encryption-at-rest, data residency, deterministic egress policy, and controlled upgrade windows.
- Ask from legal: agree on an evaluation path and a single POC scope (data classification + audit trail validation).

Slide 3 — Typical legal/controls checklist (what they care about)
- Data residency & residency guarantees (region-level, deletion semantics)
- Data plane ownership and who can access logs/KV cache
- Encryption: customer KMS/HSM support, BYOK workflows
- Auditability: structured access logs, immutable event timelines, export formats for eDiscovery
- Isolation: tenancy model (single-tenant pools, VPC flow logs, network policies)
- Change management: scheduled upgrades, rollback plan, security patch cadence
- Incident response: runbooks, SLAs for breach notification, forensic access

Slide 4 — Common objections & short responses (SE script, 15–30s each)
1) "We can’t send data to a third party."
   Response: Offer Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and network egress controls; include on-site option where network is air-gapped and Redwood provides an admin bundle for deployment.
2) "We require BYOK and HSM-backed keys."
   Response: Redwood supports customer KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for signing; show KMS/PKI architecture diagram (appendix).
3) "We need proof of non-repudiation/auditability."
   Response: Provide sample audit export (CSV/JSON) and a short demo of our immutable event timeline + SIEM integration example.
4) "What if we need to revert a model rollout?"
   Response: We support pinned model versions, canary rollouts, and documented rollback policies; include SLA on rollback windows for Dedicated contracts.

Slide 5 — Negotiation levers (practical handles to offer)
- Term & commit: extend contract term to secure reserved capacity discounts (trade for longer onboarding window).
- Support level: offer enhanced SOC2/HIPAA-ready operational runbook as a paid add-on for the pilot period.
- Data residency: agree on legal language specifying regional-only processing and exported evidence of location.
- Escrow & Source: include a limited escrow of a vetted deployment artifact for emergency continuation (controlled, auditable).

Slide 6 — Minimal POC plan (day 0–30) — customer-friendly path
- Week 0: NDA + whitelist IP + create test VPC + KMS integration checklist
- Week 1: deploy containerized runtime in customer VPC (small instance), ingest sanitized sample dataset
- Week 2: verify audit logs, key management flow, and model output QA with baseline prompt set
- Week 3: run security scan (SCA), pen test summary, and SIEM integration test
- Week 4: finalize acceptance criteria, handover to platform team for expansion plan

Slide 7 — Metrics sellers can quote on first call
- Typical pilot install time: 2–3 weeks (depending on procurement)
- Expected token latency delta vs hosted: +10–50ms median (depends on region and instance type)
- Audit log latency: near real-time (<5s ingestion to SIEM)
- Cost example (illustrative): Dedicated pool reserved 1yr commitment reduces per-token cost ~28% vs on-demand hosted (numbers vary by model & quantization)

Slide 8 — Two short customer vignettes (anonymized)
- Fintech customer: needed ledger-level residency and HSM keys. Outcome: Private VPC deployment + KMS integration; purchase moved from POC to annual reserved contract after 9 weeks.
- Health SaaS: required on-prem and air-gapped inference for a pilot. Outcome: on-prem bundle + audit report; procurement requested additional runbook for quarterly compliance checks.

Slide 9 — Technical appendix (for SEs) — short checkboxes to run during demo
- Verify TLS mTLS between control plane and runtime
- Confirm KMS key rotation handshake works with sample rotate command
- Export audit log and validate columns: timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id
- Run model rollback command and measure time-to-ready for previous version
- Demonstrate restricted outbound egress rules (show iptables/nsenter output)

Slide 10 — Legal talking points (copyable language)
- Sample SLA clause: "Redwood will provide documented procedures for scheduled upgrades and will notify the Customer no less than 14 days in advance for non-critical updates; critical security patches will be applied per the emergency change procedure with notification within 48 hours."
- Sample data residency clause: "All inference requests and associated ephemeral caches will be processed and stored only within the customer-specified cloud region(s) for the duration of the contract unless otherwise authorized in writing."

Slide 11 — Red flags to escalate to Solutions/Legal (when to pause deal)
- Customer requires permanent raw training-data retention on Redwood-managed storage.
- Customer requests unrestricted source code access beyond a scoped escrow for business continuity.
- Customer requires custom cryptographic modules that alter runtime binary semantics (introduces unverified code paths).

Slide 12 — Closing checklist for seller before procurement handoff
- Confirm chosen deployment mode (VPC / on-prem / dedicated) and region(s)
- Collect KMS owner contact and technical point-of-contact
- Confirm audit export format and SIEM endpoint details
- Lock in pilot acceptance criteria and rollback conditions in writing
- Add legal-approved substitution clauses to SOW (if needed)

Appendix A — Example audit export snippet (CSV)
- timestamp,request_id,principal,action,resource,outcome,region
- 2026-02-20T14:12:33Z,req_0145,user:svc-analytics,INFER:model-7b,completed,us-west-2

Appendix B — Quick integration references (where SEs can point to docs)
- Implementation guide: confluence.redwood/private-deployments-kms-guide (linked artifact above)
- SOC2 report access process: compliance.redwood/request-soc2
- Demo script: github.com/redwood-inference/internal/demos/private-poc

Notes to self (informal)
- We should add a short checklist page for Procurement (pricing worksheets and sample SOW clauses).
- Next revision: include a one-page risk heatmap with estimated mitigation timelines and cost to remediate.
- Action: ask legal for a small repository of approved contract snippets by 2026-03-15.

End of deck sketch — this is intentionally lean (seller + SE friendly). Keep it as an editable slides doc and iterate with Legal + Solutions before moving it into polished collateral.
